title: Atomicize interleaved response accounting and reconcile partial-retry token attribution
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary:
We observed repeated small divergences between the async streaming token ledger and final post-hoc batch accounting for interleaved multi-client sessions and partial-retry scenarios. The goal of this ticket is to design and implement an atomic ledger layer that deterministically attributes input and output tokens for interleaved/fragmented streams, supports idempotent partial retries, and surfaces concise observability so that billing and quota decisions are provably correct even under concurrent reconnects, model-switch fallbacks, and multiplexed prefixes.

Background / motivation:
- Current per-fragment accounting relies on optimistic incremental writes to the metering stream which can be duplicated on reconnects or reordered by transport.
- Several incidents (linked in updates) show 1-3% overcount errors across edge workloads (multiplexed prefix cache + model fallback), causing billing mismatches with customers and internal quota anomalies.
- Existing fixes (dedupe windows, chunk idempotency) reduced variance but do not fully cover interleaved fragments that share prefixes or when a mid-stream model switch causes different tokenization semantics.

Goals / Acceptance criteria:
1) Deterministic token attribution: for any completed session (success, canceled, or failed), the ledger must reconcile to a single token count that matches a post-hoc canonical tokenizer pass.
2) Partial-retry idempotency: repeated or overlapping partial-retries (resume, resend) must not increase customer charge beyond the intended canonical output; duplicate fragments should be detected and reconciled automatically.
3) Cross-path agreement: streaming and non-streaming (batch) accounting for the same payload must converge to identical numbers within the same release.
4) Observability: expose per-session reconciliation status and a short root-cause tag (e.g., "duplicate-fragment", "out-of-order", "model-mismatch") in the Console so support can resolve disputes quickly.
5) No single-request latency regression > 2% for typical 1-2s streaming responses.

Technical approach (high-level):
- Introduce a small atomic "metering-ledger" service that accepts idempotent ledger-append operations (session_id, fragment_id, fragment_kind, token_counts, canonical_hash). Appends are committed atomically and support conditional reconciliation ops.
- Each streaming worker will acquire a light-weight session lease and push fragment appends to the ledger instead of writing directly to the metering DB. The ledger will guarantee linearizable ordering per-session.
- Implement a reconciliation step that: 1) on session close, verifies concatenated fragments against a canonical tokenizer pass; 2) computes final credits (inputs/outputs) and performs a single commit to the metering DB; 3) emits a reconciliation event with root-cause metadata if diffs are found.
- Partial-retry handling: fragments carry a client-supplied fragment_id and a resume_nonce. The ledger will reject duplicate fragment_ids or mark them as duplicates and hold until reconciliation.
- Model-switch hazard: ledger keeps the model_version metadata per fragment. During reconciliation, if tokenization differs across fragments due to model switch, the reconciliation will follow the pinned model_version on the session or apply a configurable fallback policy (default: charge based on the model_version that produced the final active stream).

Migration / rollout plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): deploy ledger in read-only shadow mode (accepting appends but not authoritative) and run reconciliation logic to compare shadow results to existing metering for a 2% sample. Collect diffs and iterate. (1 week)
- Phase 2 (opt-in): enable ledger-as-authoritative for low-traffic workspaces with billing safety net. Monitor delta and support ticket triage. (2 weeks)
- Phase 3 (global): flip default to authoritative once deltas are within 0.1% for 48h.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for boundary cases: fragment overlap, out-of-order delivery, duplicate fragment ids, mixed model versions, and truncated final fragments.
- Integration tests: synthetic multiplexed sessions with concurrent prefix cache hits and intentional reconnects.
- Long-run fuzzy test: run a 24h synthetic workload that simulates customers with partial-retries at 2-5% frequency and validate ledger convergence.

Operational concerns:
- The ledger must be horizontally scalable and append-heavy; design for sharding by session_id and short-lived retention (retain raw fragments for 7 days for dispute handling).
- Add per-session reconciliation metrics: fragments_received, fragments_deduped, reconciliation_time_ms, token_diff_absolute, token_diff_ratio. Surface alerts when token_diff_ratio > 0.5%.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Should canonicalization always re-run the tokenizer server-side, or rely on worker-supplied canonical_hash to avoid tokenization variability? (We plan to re-run tokenizer during reconciliation to ensure determinism.)
- How aggressive should dedupe be for out-of-order fragments that arrive after reconciliation? (Current plan: hold ready fragments for a 10s window; decline late fragments and surface dispute tag.)

References & links: see updates for investigation artifacts and dashboards.
updates: 2026-03-01 - Triage: observed meter delta spike during multiplexed prefix rollout. Logged by on-call after customer report. Assigned to Mateo. Initial hypothesis: duplicate fragment appends on reconnects.

2026-03-02 - Investigation: ran sample job replaying 3k sessions; found 0.8% overcount correlated with reconnects + prefix cache hits. Notebook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/replica-overcount-analysis (internal)

2026-03-03 - Design sync: agreed on 'metering-ledger' approach with infra and runtime leads. Trade-off: small added commit path vs deterministic final accounting. Action: prototype ledger API and session lease semantics.

2026-03-05 - Prototype: lightweight in-memory ledger service implemented in runtime sandbox. Basic per-session linearizable ordering passing unit tests. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/1892
2026-03-07 - Review feedback (infra): request for strong idempotency keys and sharding plan. Also asked for metrics contract for Console. Added metrics list to ticket.

2026-03-08 - QA: reproducible test created that simulates partial-retry with model-switch. Current prototype reconciles to canonical tokenizer output for 98.7% of runs — edge cases remain when model switch changes token boundaries.

2026-03-09 - Decision: reconciliation will re-run tokenizer server-side and attach root-cause tags to reconciliation events. Blocker: tokenizer version pinning coordination with model onboarding (ENG-21450).

2026-03-10 - Next steps: implement durable ledger backed by Cockroach (POC schema in repo), add reconciliation worker and Console hooks; plan canary for 2% of production workspace traffic in Phase 1. Creating follow-up sub-tasks for rollout checklist and runbook.

2026-03-10 - Links: incident timeline & customer support notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/incident/metering-2026-02; sandbox PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/1892; reconciliation dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/meter/recon-summary
